title_en: Stories of Modern China (15/20): When the Rice Paddy Became a Factory
note_en: Chinese often marks the passive with 被, putting the doer right after it: 那片稻田被一家电子厂买走了 "the rice paddy was bought by an electronics factory." Unlike English "was bought," the verb itself doesn't change, and 被 sentences usually need a result after the verb (买走, "bought and taken away") rather than a bare verb.
